A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MultiMat research work. Their complete main texts and Appendix A, including tables, figures, equations, and program listings, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original unconditional and conditional generation results in Tables 2–3, qualitative examples, and a tree-search ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds expert preference results in Figure 5 and repair-frequency measurements in Table 4.

M1.justification: The conditioning variants, CompactSBS representation, incremental tree search, automatic repairs, and optional DiffMat optimization remain unchanged. The newly stated loss and implementation details document the existing procedure without establishing a method change.

E1.justification: Both use the same 6,878-material collection for unconditional generation and inverse material synthesis. The challenging filtered-graph scenario used by v2's human evaluation already appears in v1's qualitative evaluation; additional examples and human ratings retain this task coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated VLMaterial(SBS) baseline and its parameter-optimized variant remain unchanged. The human comparison uses the same model variants already compared qualitatively in v1. Added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New Section 6.3 introduces expert evaluation: eight annotators rank randomized output triplets for 33 challenging materials, using candidates selected by DreamSim from 40 generations. Best-of-40 selection existed for v1's qualitative figures, but the human-ranking protocol is new. Existing training and automatic-evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds an error analysis measuring parameter deletions and conversion-node insertions across models. Appendix A expands the failure examples from four to six. The tree-search ablation, including NER changing from 14.846 to 33.953 when disabled, was already present in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new human-preference percentages likewise lack uncertainty or inter-rater agreement estimates; the annotator count belongs to the evaluation protocol.

E6.justification: All scores in Tables 2–3 remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial human-preference and repair-analysis results. Figure 5 reports 83.3% preference for MultiMat+ (Mixed) and 81.1% for MultiMat+ (Graph) over VLMaterial+ (SBS), and 58.3% for Graph over Mixed. Table 4 and eight additional qualitative examples provide further new results.

T1.justification: v2 adds Equation (1), explicitly defining the node/token cross-entropy objective and its graph, image, and input conditioning variables. This is a limited mathematical definition absent from v1; no theorem, proof, or new backtracking derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The main contributions and claims about visual feedback, efficient validation/backtracking, full-feature graph representation, and superior synthesis remain intact. The abstract's change from 'syntactic validity' to 'static correctness' refines terminology for validation already described in v1.

C2.justification: v2 interprets repair frequencies as evidence of intrinsic graph understanding, explaining that corrections are not fed back to models. Its limitations discussion newly argues that small datasets keep absolute training costs acceptable and softens the inference comparison to more similar throughput.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies AdamW, states the training loss, describes the backbone's late fusion, and clarifies baseline training and validation/repair behavior. These are additional disclosures; previously reported hyperparameters, hardware, and training-duration comparisons remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Seven references are added: Thakoor, Ye, Lin, Xu, and Wen on related research, plus Loshchilov–Hutter and Thurstone for optimization and human evaluation. The research positioning remains largely unchanged. The Ebert/Musgrave book-entry revision represents the same work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized abstract and limitations edits, expands training and baseline explanations, adds Section 6.3, revises the appendix introduction, and swaps the ethics and acknowledgements order. Most existing prose and the main section structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a preference bar chart, repair table, and six-example qualitative figure, and expands the failure figure by two rows. Existing diagrams, benchmark-table designs, unconditional examples, and program listing are retained, with figure renumbering and some float relocation.

improvement.justification: The expert evaluation adds useful perceptual validation beyond v1's automatic metrics and selected examples. Repair measurements, additional failure cases, and implementation disclosures also improve transparency. These gains are limited: the human study covers 33 materials and reports neither uncertainty nor annotator agreement, while the principal benchmark evidence remains unchanged.
